item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-10cdee68f11e85f4","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Mexico's proposed Plan B electoral reform was criticized by INE participants as limiting the INE's authority to establish affirmative-action rules and reducing legislatively represented spaces for historically discriminated groups from 65 to 25; critics said the allocation lacked contextual analysis, clear criteria, certainty, and judicial or administrative independence.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.4","4B.7","4B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published February 8, 2023; directly relevant to AMLO's 2023 electoral reform agenda.","ruler_attribution":"The source reports criticism of the government's Plan B reform but does not establish that AMLO personally authored every provision.","limitations":["Institutional criticism and expert assessments are reported; the source does not provide a court judgment or final implementation record."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f03a2862f2f7bb5c","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The UN Committee on Enforced Disappearances reported that Mexico's national registry recorded 111,540 disappeared or missing persons through September 12, 2023, raised concerns that updates did not follow the standardized search protocol, and called for transparent methodology, independent and impartial coordination, victim-collective participation, and protection against revictimization.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.7","3B.10","7B.2"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"UN observations issued October 3, 2023 and include data through September 12, 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern the Mexican state during AMLO's presidency; personal attribution to AMLO is not separately demonstrated.","limitations":["The source summarizes committee observations rather than documenting which individual official caused each failure."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f03a2862f2f7bb5c","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The UN Committee expressed concern about inadequate investigations into the alarming number of disappearances, very low conviction rates, and almost absolute impunity, urging Mexico to investigate promptly, impartially, and thoroughly and prosecute and punish those responsible.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.6","3B.9","3B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The committee's country observations were issued in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The assessment concerns state performance under the AMLO administration but does not assign personal responsibility for individual cases.","limitations":["The supplied text does not quantify changes from the inherited baseline or identify specific corrective actions taken by AMLO."]},{"source_id":"SRC-468305ab629fd8dd","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"IMCO reported that corruption risks in federal public procurement increased from 2021 to 2022 in 184 of 260 institutions, with a federal competition-risk score of 70/100; 38% of procurement spending was directly awarded, 25% of tenders had three or fewer participants, and substantial contracting information was missing or published late.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.5","5B.6","5B.7","7B.6","7B.9","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published July 17, 2023 using federal procurement data for 2022, within AMLO's 2023 governing period.","ruler_attribution":"The findings concern federal procurement institutions under AMLO's government; they do not prove AMLO personally directed each procurement.","limitations":["The report identifies systemic and institutional risks, not final findings of corruption or personal enrichment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-468305ab629fd8dd","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"IMCO reported that federal institutions awarded contracts to sanctioned suppliers and shell companies, that 74% of medicine spending was directly awarded, and that Diconsa directly awarded 90% of its 19.734 billion pesos in procurement; it recommended strengthening competition, supplier information, and oversight.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","7B.9","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The 2023 index evaluates 2022 procurement and was published during 2023.","ruler_attribution":"These are federal-system findings during AMLO's administration, not proof that AMLO personally selected the suppliers.","limitations":["The supplied page reports risk indicators and recommendations, not adjudicated criminal or administrative liability."]},{"source_id":"SRC-52609fc7eb4d9218","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"RSF reported that President López Obrador and other state figures used violent and stigmatizing rhetoric against journalists, including a weekly government segment intended to discredit the press; it also reported that threats and attacks, rather than formal censorship laws, constrained journalism, while authorities had not undertaken needed reforms against violence and impunity.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"RSF's Mexico 2023 country assessment concerns the period of AMLO's presidency.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the rhetoric and weekly government segment to López Obrador and his government.","limitations":["RSF describes the context and reported pattern but the supplied text does not provide a complete incident-level dataset."]},{"source_id":"SRC-678c004011e531fb","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Transparency International's supplied CPI page states that Mexico is included in the 2022 corruption-perceptions index but provides no Mexico-specific score or country assessment in the extracted units.","question_ids":["5B.5","7B.1","7B.10"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The page concerns CPI 2022 and was available for the 2023 evaluation period.","ruler_attribution":"No specific attribution to AMLO is supported by the supplied units.","limitations":["The extracted document lacks the Mexico-specific score, rank, trend, methodology application, or country narrative."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5672debc6285a38c","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"Mexico's APECIC anti-inflation program, announced October 3, 2022 and extended through February 2023, sought an 8% reduction in prices for 24 basic goods through an agreement with 15 private companies, while granting participating firms temporary exemptions from import procedures and permits.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.9","6B.1","6B.2","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The program covered part of 2023 but was announced in October 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The report identifies the Office of the President and the Government of Mexico; AMLO was president and presented the agreement.","limitations":["The report is an unofficial translation and does not establish whether the promised price reduction was achieved."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5672debc6285a38c","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"APECIC transferred responsibility for verifying imported goods' health, safety, and quality from normal regulatory procedures to participating companies, suspended review of regulations that could raise food-import costs, froze selected fuel, electricity, and highway rates, and authorized consumer-protection verification and sanctions.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.4","5B.5","5B.6","5B.9","6B.2","6B.5","8B.2","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The measures were scheduled through February 28, 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures were commitments of the Government of Mexico under the presidential agreement.","limitations":["The supplied text does not report enforcement results, consumer outcomes, or whether the Federal Register decree was ultimately published."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b8940b5a4a857efe","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"A May 2023 opinion article argued that AMLO's administration was blocking the INAI and pursuing opacity, linking this to his earlier opposition as Mexico City head to an autonomous transparency framework, including a veto, a constitutional challenge, and delayed funding for the local information council.","question_ids":["4B.2","4B.4","4B.6","4B.10","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published May 2, 2023; it combines 2023 claims with historical conduct from 2000-2003.","ruler_attribution":"The article directly attributes the reported positions and actions to López Obrador.","limitations":["This is an explicitly argumentative opinion article; some historical claims are presented by the author rather than independently verified in the supplied text."]},{"source_id":"SRC-35dc4d5df00e9a4e","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"México Evalúa reported that federal spending differed substantially from the Congress-approved budget because of discretionary executive decisions, that 40% of approved budget programs experienced substantial cuts, and that spending was advanced toward politically favored transfers and projects while health funding for people without social security declined.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.7","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Published May 26, 2022 and based on first-quarter 2022 budget data; it is pre-2023 context for AMLO's continuing administration.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the decisions to the federal executive under AMLO.","limitations":["The source is not a 2023 outcome assessment and does not establish whether the budget pattern continued unchanged through all of 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-73ddd05d8aef0338","start_unit":2,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Mexico, under López Obrador's stated proposal, advocated a diplomatic caucus involving the UN Secretary-General and other leaders to promote confidence-building and mediation between Russia and Ukraine; it also emphasized preventive diplomacy, humanitarian assistance, accountability for Security Council vetoes, arms-trafficking controls, and nuclear disarmament.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.4","1B.8","1B.10","2B.1","2B.7","2B.10","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The speech was delivered September 22, 2022 and describes Mexico's position during López Obrador's presidency, providing 2023-relevant foreign-policy context.","ruler_attribution":"The foreign minister explicitly presented the proposal as López Obrador's initiative and Mexico's policy.","limitations":["The document records advocacy and diplomatic positioning, not proof that the proposed caucus was created or achieved a settlement."]},{"source_id":"SRC-114805f9ea1298a0","start_unit":1,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Mexico delivered a joint statement on behalf of Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons parties and signatories, reaffirming commitment to the NPT, nuclear disarmament, the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty, risk-reduction measures, verification, negative security assurances, and a fissile-material prohibition.","question_ids":["1B.1","1B.2","1B.4","1B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Statement delivered August 17, 2022; relevant as Mexico's formal policy posture entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The statement was delivered by Mexico's ambassador on behalf of the government; personal direction by AMLO is not separately shown.","limitations":["The statement establishes diplomatic commitments and advocacy, not domestic implementation, funding, or measurable risk reduction."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied corpus contains mostly institutional reports, media assessments, and policy statements; it does not provide comprehensive evidence for every 1B-8B question.","Several sources concern 2022 or earlier events and therefore provide contextual evidence rather than direct full-year 2023 outcome evidence.","No fact is scored; polarity reflects the direction of the reported fact, not a chapter judgment."]}
